basis: Renal cystic disease; hepatic cysts occur in 6/8, but clinically significant hepatic damage affects <30%. Cysts alone do not establish impaired liver function.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic cysts occur in 75%, but usually preserve function; damaging or functionally significant hepatic disease occurs in <30%.

basis: Ectrodactyly and ectodermal dysplasia define the syndrome; damaging dental abnormalities in ≥30% are not established for this specific condition.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental defects are possible in ectodermal dysplasia, but common damaging dental involvement is not established for this specific syndrome.

basis: Sodium-losing enteropathy causes defining electrolyte/acid-base disturbances; syndromic choanal atresia and recurrent corneal erosions each occur in >30%.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia is a characteristic structural airway obstruction reported in >30% of syndromic cases.
decisions.ocular: involved: recurrent corneal erosions directly injure the cornea and occur in >30% of syndromic cases.

basis: Microtia and aortic/cardiac malformations define the syndrome; CNS malformations/developmental impairment and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: hydrocephalus, posterior fossa abnormalities and developmental impairment occur in 30-79%; ear and aortic abnormalities define the core syndrome.

basis: GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with intellectual disability and seizures; distal phalangeal shortening occurs in 80-99%. Renal and ocular abnormalities occur in <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal phalangeal shortening is a direct skeletal malformation present in 80-99%; metabolic and neurologic abnormalities define the core disorder.

basis: Venom directly disrupts neural function; cardiac conduction dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Local erythema/edema are transient; pulmonary edema occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: common local pain, erythema and edema are transient sting reactions; substantial skin injury is not established.

basis: Clonal blood-cell glycosylation defect exposes Tn antigen, enabling antibody-mediated polyagglutination and immune destruction of affected blood cells.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: antibody recognition of exposed Tn antigen mediates the defining polyagglutination; this supports an immune mechanism alongside the blood-cell defect.

basis: Restrictive skin disease; skeletal malformations include short clavicles in 2/2. Rectal prolapse occurs in 1/2. Respiratory distress and proptosis alone do not establish organ damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: short clavicles occur in 2/2 and abnormal long bones in 1/2; these are associated skeletal malformations of the defining restrictive skin disorder.

basis: ID, metaphyseal dysplasia and optic atrophy occur in 2/2; GI atresia/bleeding in 1/2. Cutaneous vascular findings and thyroid dysfunction omitted at cap; tiny series.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cutaneous telangiectasia occurs in 2/2, but retained neurologic, skeletal, ocular and gastrointestinal disease has stronger evidence of consequential damage; cap applied.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: anal atresia and gastrointestinal hemorrhage each occur in 1/2; these establish direct structural or bleeding involvement.
decisions.ocular: primary: eye abnormalities are explicitly defining, with optic atrophy in 2/2 and documented visual impairment.

basis: Gingival fibromatosis in 9/9 defines oral disease; nonspecific sternal morphology in 3/9 (~33%) does not establish skeletal damage or dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: abnormal sternal morphology in 3/9 (~33%) meets the frequency threshold, but the unspecified finding does not establish damaging skeletal involvement.
